final_evidence.section: Get to the eastern Fairy Fountain
final_evidence.text:
[Get to the eastern Fairy Fountain]
The blue candle can be used to burn trees to reveal secrets. Such secrets are never on the edge of the screen: save time and spare those poor trees.
Go one screen west and then follow the river north. In the next screen you're on Lake Hylia. Follow the coast east.
In the next screen there are six trees in the middle. Use the candle to burn the lower-left one, and you'll get 10 Rupees.
Follow the coast of Lake Hylia one screen north and one east. On this screen burn the fifth tree from the right, and you'll find a fourth Heart Container . Do not choose the potion: that can be purchased elsewhere, but the heart container is unique.
On the next screen, burn the trees in the upper-right corner to find 30 Rupees.
Walk one screen south to leave the Hylia lakeshore and enter the green forest. Walk one screen east, then two screens north, and you'll get to the eastern Fairy Fountain.

- Level 1: Boomerang & Bow
- Level 2: Magic Boomerang

final_evidence.text:
[Money Making Game]
Immediately to the left of the start screen, there is a rock face that can be bombed to reveal a cave where the money making game can be repeatedly played. If you lose or gain a lot of rupees, press Start to access the weapons screen. Then, on the second controller, press Up (D-pad) and A simultaneously. The game will immediately end, bringing you to the "CONTINUE", "RETRY" or "SAVE" option. If you've lost money, select "RETRY" and you'll be back at the start screen, with your previous rupee count intact. If you've been lucky and gained a lot of rupees, select "SAVE" and you'll go back to the character select screen. In either case, the total number of replays for your character will not advance and you can quickly move back to the money making game to maximize your earnings.

[(intro)]
The game has been re-released in several formats over the years. In 1994, Nintendo released the game in cartridge format for the first time in Japan, towards the end of the Famicom's lifetime. In 1999, it was remade by fans to MS-DOS (and later Windows) as Zelda Classic, containing an editor. In 2003, the game was released for the Nintendo GameCube as part of The Legend of Zelda: Collector's Edition. In 2004, the game was released for the Game Boy Advance as part of the Classic NES Series. In 2006, the game was announced to be one of the first Wii Virtual Console titles. In 2011, it was available for download through the Nintendo eShop for use with the 3DS Virtual Console. In 2013, the eShop release was made available to the Wii U Virtual Console.

[Walkthrough > Dungeon Walkthrough]
- The entrance to this dungeon is found on Lake Hylia (at A-4 of section 3), just over the bridge which is a short distance north from where you begin the game.
- Start by clearing the rooms both right (Q-6) and left (O-6) of the entrance to obtain two Keys.
- At this point there is a glitch where if you leave the dungeon and re-enter, the first locked door is unlocked.
- Clear the next two rooms above the entrance (to P-4). The north wall in the room can be bombed to reveal a hidden pathway and save one Key.
- In the room past the hidden pathway (P-3) you'll encounter some Gels guarding a Map.
- From the map room, go left to arrive in room O-3 with a single block. The door to the left can be opened by moving the block in any direction once all of the monsters are cleared. The room to the left contains a man who gives you a hint as to the whereabouts of a secret stash of rupees (in the north-eastern corner of the overworld): "Eastmost peninsula is the secret."

[Old Woman]
Many women make their homes in Hyrule's caves and trees. It is common for the women of Hyrule to know the secrets to making the Water of Life, a Hyrulian recipe that restores the strength of those who drink it. However, they only sell this concoction to those who present the special Letter to them. Other women in Hyrule offer important information about the nearby vicinity, but sometimes only after being well compensated.

← Section 6 | Section 2 →
[1st Quest]
A-1: See Section 3
B-1: This is one of the magical lakes where a life refilling fairy lives. Visit here to restore your health.
C-1: See Section 3
A-2: Burn the topmost tree along the right border to reveal a cave where you can receive 30 rupees.
B-2: This is one of the secret passage exits. You must have the Power Bracelet in order to move the rock which opens the entrance to the passage. The passage links to the other exits in Section 1, Section 7, and directly to the south.
C-2: The store inside of the cave sells (the ability to use) Arrows for 80 rupees, the Magical Shield for 130 rupees, and a set of 4 Bombs for 20 rupees.
D-2: Burn one of the trees closest to the entrance to the desert to find a stairwell that leads to a medicine woman. If you've shown her the Letter, you can buy Red Potions for 68 rupees, and Water of Lifes for 40 rupees.
D-3: If you burn down the lower solitary tree on the left, you will reveal a stairwell that leads to 10 Rupees.
A-4: By burning the bottom leftmost tree, you will discover a stairwell, but the man inside will charge you 20 rupees for repairs.

[(intro)]

Section 6 →
[1st Quest]
A-1: See Section 7
C-1: "There are secrets where fairies don't live" and this lake is peculiar for not having a fairy. A few notes on the Whistle will reveal the location of the seventh dungeon.
D-1: This is a lake where one of the life granting fairies live.
E-1: See Section 6
B-2: By burning down the lower right tree, you will reveal a stairwell that leads to 10 Rupees.
B-3: This is the Lost Woods. Only by passing through the woods in the proper sequence, can you hope to escape to the west. By paying the woman in the lower left corner of Hyrule, you can learn that sequence: North, West, South, West.
C-3: The tree at the top of the single column of trees can be burned down to reveal a stairwell, where a Red Moblin will give Link 100 Rupees. The stairwell can also serve as a shortcut between the two sections of this area.
D-3: If you burn the lower tree just left of center, you will find a stairwell, but the man inside will charge you 20 rupees for repairs.

[1st Quest]
C-4: Burn the bottom solitary tree, and you will reveal another stairwell, but the man who lives there will charge you 20 rupees for repairs.
D-4: Burn down the bottom center tree among the group of trees on the right to find a stairwell. Venture down the stairs to find a Red Moblin that is willing to part with 100 Rupees.
A-5: Burn down the bottom center tree among the group of trees on the left to reveal a stairwell that leads to a medicine woman. If you've shown her the Letter, you can buy Red Potions for 68 rupees, and Water of Lifes for 40 rupees.
B-5: This is one of the secret passage exits. You must have the Power Bracelet in order to move the rock which opens the entrance to the passage. The passage links to the other exits in Section 1, Section 7, and directly to the north.
D-5: If you bomb the wall to the left of the north path, you will reveal a cave where you can obtain a Heart Container.

[Old Man (Overworld)]
A variety of men live in Hyrule's overworld as well. Like the women of Hyrule, they may dispense information. Hyrulian men are also fond of gambling and will play the Money Making game with anyone who will part with their rupees. There are also some old men, who live in well hidden caves, who will give Link a Red Water of Life or a Heart Container of his choice. However, some men of Hyrule prefer to be left alone. If you reveal their location by destroying their secret entrance, expect to be forced to compensate them for the repairs.
